title: Avvaiyar and the Jamun Tree
director: claude-opus-5-5 (authored in Claude Code, same rules as scripts/audio/direct.ts)

cast.name: Avvaiyar
cast.description: Elderly, celebrated woman poet, dignified, a little proud, then humbled

cast.name: The cowherd boy
cast.description: Young boy, playful, mischievous, secretly divine

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Welcome to LitBridge, where stories cross languages. Today's story comes from the Tamil tradition. It is a legend about Avvaiyar, the most celebrated poet of the Tamil land. It is called... Avvaiyar and the Jamun Tree.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Avvaiyar was the most celebrated poet of the Tamil land. Kings sought her advice, and scholars bowed when she entered a court. She had begun to believe there was nothing left that anyone could teach her.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One hot afternoon, walking a long road, she sat down to rest under a jamun tree. High in the branches, a cowherd boy sat swinging his legs.

lines.speaker: boy
lines.text: [playful] Paati! Grandmother, you look tired. Would you like some fruit?

lines.speaker: boy
lines.text: [mischievous] Do you want hot fruit... or cold fruit?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Avvaiyar frowned. Fruit was fruit. Was the boy mocking her? But she was curious.

lines.speaker: avvaiyar
lines.text: [amused, testing] Give me hot fruit, then.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The boy shook a branch, and ripe purple jamuns fell into the sand. Avvaiyar picked one up and, as anyone would, blew on it to clear away the dust.

lines.speaker: boy
lines.text: [laughs] Is it very hot, Paati? You have to blow on it to cool it down!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [softly] The poet sat very still. She who had answered the riddles of kings had been out-witted by a child with a mouthful of fruit.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [awed] She looked up to praise him... and saw that he was no cowherd. The god Murugan sat in the branches, smiling, a peacock at his side.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Avvaiyar folded her hands. She understood that learning has no end, and that wisdom can come from the youngest voice in the shade.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [gently] It is a story about humility. The wisest are those who remember they can still be taught. Thank you for listening to LitBridge.
